transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... I guess I came in because I've been having a hard time. Once a worry starts... I just can't seem to shelve it in my mind. 

It's usually just normal things, like my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or worrying I missed something at work. But I make lists, and I try to redirect myself, and... it just doesn't really stop.
Do these worries happen even when you're not around other people or in social situations?
Yes. Um... it doesn't really matter if anyone is around. I could just be sitting at home by myself, and... they're still there.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms along with these worries, like feeling restless, being easily fatigued, or having muscle tension?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. Mostly just... tension. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel pretty locked up. Just from bracing myself, I guess. And... I do catch myself clenching my jaw sometimes. Usually just when I'm answering emails, or... listening out for my mother in the next room.
Have you noticed that you have trouble concentrating or that your mind goes blank because of these worries?

Um... yeah, sometimes. Mostly at work. Like... during cataloging reviews, or in staff meetings. I'll be looking right at the screen, or the agenda, and... I just suddenly realize I haven't absorbed a single word. My mind just sort of... wanders off into some problem I think I should have prevented, I guess.
Do you find that you worry about a number of different things, even if they’re not necessarily serious or urgent?

Um... yes. I guess it's a lot of things. It used to just be... worrying about my mother being safe. But over the last year, it's... it's just spread. 

I worry about money, and... decisions with the staff at the library. Deadlines. Things around the house. Even just... whether I'm doing enough for my mother. It just feels like even the little things are... I don't know, about to unravel.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends?
Um... no, not really. I mean... I still like reading, when I have the time. And I don't feel hopeless, exactly. Just... worried. Mostly just worried.
Have you noticed any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is too active with worries?

Um... yes. Sleep is... it's difficult. 

Most nights, I just... I lie there. Replaying everything that happened during the day. Trying to plan for every possible problem that could come up. And... if I hear my mother moving around in the night, I wake up. And then I'm awake for... maybe an hour or two. 

I just... I usually get to the library feeling like I didn't really sleep at all.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable lately, especially when you're dealing with these worries?
Um... I don't know. Maybe a little. I just... I get tired, you know? But I wouldn't say I'm... angry or anything. Just... tired.
Have you been worrying like this — almost every day — for at least six months?
Um... yes. It's been... a while. About a year and two months, I think. That's when... my mother moved in with me, after she had a fall. It's just been... like this, since then.
